title: Social Cognition: Attribution & Attribution Errors
summary: Attribution theory: Heider's naive psychology, Kelley's covariation model, fundamental attribution error and actor-observer bias. How people explain causes of behaviour.
objectives: Define fundamental attribution error and actor-observer bias.
revision: Attribution: Heider's theory, Kelley's covariation model, fundamental attribution error and actor-observer bias.

notes.t: The process by which people explain the causes of behaviour — their own and others'.
Fritz Heider proposed that people act as naive scientists, attributing behaviour to either internal (dispositional) or external (situational) causes.
Harold Kelley's model: people attribute behaviour to causes that covary with it, using consensus, distinctiveness and consistency information.
The tendency to overestimate dispositional (internal) causes and underestimate situational (external) causes for others' behaviour.
The tendency to attribute one's own behaviour to situational causes but others' behaviour to dispositional causes.
These biases show that attribution is not purely rational — cognitive shortcuts and perspectives shape causal explanations.
UGC NET frequently asks about Heider's attribution theory, Kelley's covariation model and the fundamental attribution error.

mnemonics.title: HKFA
mnemonics.text: H — Heider (internal/external causes), K — Kelley (consensus, distinctiveness, consistency), F — fundamental attribution error, A — actor-observer bias

flashcards.a: Overestimate dispositional, underestimate situational for others.
